headline: Data Center Grid Cost Responsibility
short_summary: This bill aims to shift certain grid infrastructure costs onto large energy users, including data centers, to reduce residential electricity bills.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Virginia bill aims to cut residential energy costs by shifting expenses to data centers
news_summary: This bill seeks to shift energy costs onto data centers, which currently consume about 20% of Dominion Energy's grid, potentially saving residential customers over $5.50 a month. While supported by Dominion Energy and some lawmakers, the data center coalition has expressed concerns about the language and its impact on their costs.

headline: Data Center Water Use Transparency
short_summary: This legislation mandates data centers to report their water consumption, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board, increasing transparency on their environmental impact.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups (Potomac Conservancy, Chesapeake Bay Foundation, Southern Environmental Law Center, Appalachian Voices), local communities, water conservation advocates, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Data center industry (due to reporting burden/potential scrutiny).
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, SB 553, mandates local water authorities to report data center water usage, making the information publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to provide transparency amid concerns about the industry's water consumption, with the reporting website expected to be live by January 1, 2027.

headline: Local Data Center Siting Control
short_summary: This bill empowers localities to require site assessments for new data centers, including noise studies, and allows examination of impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites, giving local governments more control over development.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups, Del. Joshua Thomas.
news_headline: Virginia, home to hundreds of data centers, adds new restrictions
news_summary: Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger signed bills, including HB 153, to regulate data centers by adding new restrictions on siting and noise. This bill allows localities to require site assessments for new high energy use facilities, examining sound profiles and potential impacts on various resources.
